title: R: the only unit a trader needs

x.post:
You made $500. Nice?

Risked $100 to make it: +5R.
Risked $2,000 to make it: +0.25R.

Same dollars. Very different trade. R is what you lose if your stop hits, and it's the only ruler that measures every trade the same way.

instagram.caption:
You made $500. Proud? Depends what you risked. On $100 risk that's +5R. On $2,000 it's +0.25R.

R is what you lose if your stop gets hit. You set it before you buy, then you measure everything with it.

How to get 1R:
1R = (entry − stop) × shares
Entry $50, stop $48, 50 shares: 1R = $100
Price gets to $58: that's +4R
Stopped out instead: −1R

We counted 20 simulated trades in R: every loser was −1R, the total was +3.5R. That's $350 if 1R is $100, or $35,000 if 1R is $10,000. R doesn't care which account it is.

If a loss ever shows up as −3R, your stop was more of a suggestion. Or price gapped past it. Either way, find out why.

Lore 003 · R: the only unit a trader needs. Next up, Lore 004: Legend 01, Jesse Livermore.

Save this for the next time a trade feels big or small and you're not sure which.

A myth card strikes out 'Lost $300? Eh, one bad trade' and shows −3R. The rule: count R, not dollars.

youtube.description:
You made $500. On $100 risk that's +5R. On $2,000 risk it's +0.25R. Same dollars, very different trade.
R is what you lose if your stop gets hit: (entry − stop) × shares, set before you buy.

Measure every result with that one ruler. Entry $50, stop $48, 50 shares: 1R = $100, and $58 is +4R. Losers should all be −1R; a −3R means the stop moved or price gapped through it. Counting in R also makes accounts comparable: +3.5R is $350 on a $10,000 account risking 1% and $35,000 on $1,000,000.

Before this: Lore 002, 35% winners can beat 60% winners.

Sources: R-multiples as popularised by Van K. Tharp, Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom (1998); R-multiple framework (luxalgo.com/library/concept/r-multiple-framework); stop orders can fill below the stop in fast markets (finra.org, investor.gov). The 20 trades are simulated: sims/r_multiples.py, seed 3 (github.com/TheTapeLore/studio).
